title: Empirical Validation of Solomonoff Prior Predictions in Toy Language Models

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Tests whether neural networks exhibit Solomonoff-like simplicity bias. While theoretically interesting for agent foundations, the practical link to alignment outcomes is indirect. Even if the bias holds, it does not directly tell us how to build safer systems.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Generating synthetic datasets of varying compressibility is feasible. Training a small GPT and measuring convergence speed is standard. The main challenge is rigorously measuring Kolmogorov complexity (which is uncomputable; LZ77 is a proxy). Medium compute is sufficient.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multiple datasets of varying complexity, training runs on each, plus OOD generalization tests. Could be narrowed to 3-4 complexity levels with just convergence speed as the metric to fit 30 hours.
